newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Pliva says share repurchase not imminent.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Pliva says share repurchase not imminent.

text.p: Croatian drugs firm Pliva said on Wednesday its plans to repurchase up to five percent of the company stock were not imminent and could take a long time to materialise.
"For now we have no intention to buy back shares," company information director Tamara Pecarevic-Susanj told Reuters.
She said the reason Pliva would seek approval for the repurchase from shareholders at a general meeting in November was "to have the situation prepared when such a need arises".
Its decision was motivated by a wish to place free funds into selected stocks, taking advantage of higher yields in such investments than in short-term loans and deposits.
Pecarevic-Susanj confirmed Pliva also wanted to form a portfolio of treasury shares which would be awarded to its management and employees.

Pliva's shares were flat at 13,000 kuna on Zagreb's bourse today. Its global depositary receipts (GDRs) traded within a $50$/50.50 range on the London Stock Exchange. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
